_meta.generated_by: AI-generated (Claude Code), 2026-11-14, on the experimental branch data-lab. Not reviewed by a person or by a combustion specialist.
_meta.what_this_is: An inference map for one question: what the documents held by the team say would have to be known before a material-flammability criterion could be set for a lunar habitat, and what the held items and PSI tests show of it. It is not a criterion, not a research plan of the team and not a prediction. Every claim, reason, closing step and verification statement is a copy of a reference item (field 'quote', the sentence as printed; or field 'text', the team's wording of the document in references.json) or of a PSI record field.
_meta.question: What would have to be established before a material-flammability criterion could be set for a lunar habitat (oxygen 30% or more, pressure 10.2 psi or less, lunar gravity)?
_meta.authorship: The choice of links, their parents, the required conditions of each link and the evidence items listed for it are the team's (AI) reading of the items. The documents do not arrange their questions as a tree.

state_rule.conditions: The conditions an evidence item states are those of its rows in data/pipeline/findings.csv (findings.py tags only conditions the item itself states; an oxygen number that is a result, such as a limit, is not a condition). An item with no row in findings.csv states no condition. A counted PSI test is a row of data/pipeline/need_tests.csv with objective_link 'stated' for a need of the link; its conditions are its recorded values in data/pipeline/tests.csv.

axes.o2: inside if the stated or recorded oxygen (both ends of a stated range) is at least the environment's lower bound
axes.pressure: inside if the stated or recorded pressure (both ends of a stated range) is at most the environment's upper bound in kPa, both rounded to 3 decimals
axes.gravity: inside if the environment's gravity level is one of the levels the item states, or the level recorded for the test
axes.flow: inside if the item states a flow speed or the test records one; the environment states no flow range

result.established: at least one row of an evidence item of kind 'result' in findings.csv, or at least one counted PSI test, is inside on every required condition of the link
result.partly: not established, and at least one evidence item or counted PSI test is held for the link (at other conditions, or stating fewer of the conditions)
result.missing: no evidence item and no counted PSI test is held for the link

specification.established: at least one evidence item of type 'requirement' in references.json is inside on every required condition
specification.partly: not established, and at least one evidence item is held (a design value or definition at the conditions counts here, not as established)

state_rule.reading: A state says what the held items and tests state, by this rule. It is the team's reading. It is not a judgement of the strength of a result, and 'established' does not mean that NASA considers the question closed.

_meta.years: The year of a document is the year written in its id, version or title in references.json; the script checks it. 'not stated in references.json' where none is written there. The year of the PSI record is its releaseDate.

stated_by.quote: Moon Base and pressurized-rover atmosphere expected between spacesuit and Earth conditions: oxygen likely 30% or more, pressure 10.2 psi or less.
Test 1 is conducted in the most severe environment expected in the spacecraft, currently 30% oxygen at 10.2 psia.

walked_path.question: Is the normal-gravity screening test conservative in microgravity?
walked_path.note: The steps are in the order of the procedure, not in the order of the years; a proposal fed back to the criterion (CP2003.prev.margin) is older than the results.

items.quote: The purpose of this test is to determine if a material, when exposed to a standard ignition source, will self-extinguish and not transfer burning debris, which can ignite adjacent materials.
Test 1 shall evaluate the candidate material in the worst-case atmosphere to which the material could be exposed.
A material is self-extinguishing if no specimen burns more than 15 cm and no specimen propagates a flame by transfer of burning debris.
More understanding on relationship between 1-g test methods to microgravity performance.
Is the NASA STD 6001, Test 1 configuration conservative or non-conservative in assessing material flammability in reduced gravity

BASS–II tests the hypothesis that materials in microgravity, with adequate ventilation, burn as well if not better than the same material in normal gravity with other conditions being identical (pressure, O2
concentration, temperature, etc.).
However, it may not be conservative for flammability in space.

One objective of the BASS–II tests is to identify what is the worst case for material flammability in spacecraft environments, and how does that compare to the terrestrial upward burning used to screen the materials for safe use aboard spacecraft.
Many of the tests focused on finding a minimum oxygen concentration or flow velocity where a material will burn in space, to compare with the Earth-based limits.

BASS-II PMMA: minimum oxygen concentration in the flammability boundary from the concurrent (stagnation-flow) rod tests 13.6% O2; minimum flammable value for the opposed-flow rods 16.3% O2 (no comparable boundary was obtained for opposed flow); normal-gravity PMMA extinction limits 17% O2 (downward spread) and 15.4% O2 (upward spread).
Test 1 is not conservative: materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.

Oxygen margins of safety (low-gravity limit minus 1g limit, % O2 by mole) were negative by as much as -5.75 (lunar gravity, Mylar G at 10.2 psia); the largest at Martian gravity was -3.35 (Nomex HT90-40) and at 0g -4.1 (Mylar G). Normal-gravity screening tests may not be conservative. The low-g limits come from 5 s drop tests and their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1g.

The specific objectives of these three experiments are to (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.
The objective of the tests to be conducted on Saffire-II is to investigate the low-gravity Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC) flammability limits in long-term low gravity.
Quantifying the difference in flammability limits for large samples is the objective of the Saffire-II experiments.
